title: Dividing a Segment in a Ratio
short: Find the point that splits a segment in the ratio a : b.
trouble: Students go a/b of the way instead of a/(a + b) of the way.

blocks.html: The midpoint from Distance and Midpoint Formulas splits a segment in the ratio $1 : 1$. Sometimes you need a point that splits it in another ratio, like $2 : 3$. The side-splitting idea from The Triangle Proportionality Theorem shows how.

Draw the right triangle under $\overline{AB}$, with legs along the grid. A point $P$ on $\overline{AB}$ with $AP : PB = a : b$ cuts the hypotenuse into $a + b$ equal parts and keeps $a$ of them. Lines through $P$ parallel to the legs cut the legs in the same ratio (the triangles are similar), so $P$ is $\frac{a}{a + b}$ of the way along in $x$ and in $y$. Its coordinates $(x, y)$ are $$x = x_1 + \tfrac{a}{a + b}(x_2 - x_1)$$ $$y = y_1 + \tfrac{a}{a + b}(y_2 - y_1)$$

blocks.name: geo-fig
blocks.cap: $AP : PB = 2 : 3$, so $P$ is $\frac{2}{5}$ of the way from $A$ to $B$, in both $x$ and $y$.

opts.label: Point P two fifths of the way from A to B

blocks.html: To divide $\overline{AB}$ so that $AP : PB = a : b$, go $\frac{a}{a + b}$ of the way from $A$ to $B$: add that fraction of the change in $x$ to $x_1$, and of the change in $y$ to $y_1$.

blocks.title: On a number line
blocks.q: $A$ is at $-3$ and $B$ is at $17$. Find $P$ with $AP : PB = 1 : 4$.
steps: There are $1 + 4 = 5$ parts, and $P$ is $\frac{1}{5}$ of the way from $A$.

blocks.title: On the coordinate plane
steps: $P$ is $\frac{2}{5}$ of the way. The change is $\langle 10, 5 \rangle$, and $\frac{2}{5}$ of it is $\langle 4, 2 \rangle$.

blocks.title: A fraction answer
steps: $P$ is $\frac{3}{4}$ of the way. The change is $\langle 6, -6 \rangle$; three quarters of it is $\left\langle \frac{9}{2}, -\frac{9}{2} \right\rangle$.

blocks.html: Going $\frac{a}{b}$ of the way instead of $\frac{a}{a + b}$. With $AP : PB = 2 : 3$, the point is $\frac{2}{5}$ of the way, not $\frac{2}{3}$: the ratio compares the two pieces with each other, but you need a piece compared with the whole. Check: $AP$ and $PB$ should come out in the ratio you were given.
